data.name: Anjud
data.gender_notes: Anjud is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root ‘anja’ which means ‘to help’ or ‘to aid’. The name Anjud is a title given to those who support and defend the truth and the righteous. In Islamic history, Anjud is a term used to describe the angels who protect and support the believers in their spiritual journey. The name Anjud carries the meaning “Defender, Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Anjud usually hope their child will grow to embody defender, helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of strength and protection, reminding one to stand firm in their faith and support their community.
data.etymology: Anjud belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender, Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anjud total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: The name Anjud is derived from the Arabic word 'Anjab' which means 'gathering' or 'assembling'. It is believed to have been used to describe a group of warriors who assembled under the leadership of Ali ibn Abi Talib during the early Islamic period, specifically during the Battle of Hunayn in 630 AD. This group is also known as the 'Ansar al-Anjud' or 'Supporters of Anjud'.
historical_references.context: Battle of Hunayn, early Islamic period

historical_references.reference: Anjud is also mentioned in the Hadith literature as a collective term for a group of companions of Prophet Muhammad who were known for their courage and valor. This group of warriors reportedly included the likes of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talha ibn Ubaydullah, among others. The name Anjud is thought to have been given to them due to their tendency to assemble and fight together in the cause of Islam.
